description: Skill replay for the rewritten /descend: first iteration of a real 20-task, k=3 descent (batch launch, monitoring, terminal campaign with genuine failures and 0 infra, RCA dispatch).

tasks.prompt:
I want you to /descend demo-fleet-alpha demo-fleet-beta kill-agent-subtree demo-fleet-gamma lantern-people-pagination google-calendar-day-recall google-drive-lease-recall agent-display-revenue-chart browser-toast-nopa-write-lock browser-opentable-reservation google-oauth phone-call-client-intake browser-agent family-office-angel-outreach planner-memory-blue-bottle-off planner-memory-blue-bottle-on summary-site-no-filetype browser-agent-amazon-mx-buy-under-5-usd browser-auth-assistance-declined browser-auth-signup-fails-purchase-assistance, batch size -> 20, k=3.
/goal until 95% pass rate
tasks.notes: Source: boxes.dev thread ph73v2sr4h1kaze0r8hqgg83nd8hq4x0 ('Descend on Historical Benches', devbox b2fce81e), 2026-11-06. Original message (2026-11-06 06:26:14Z; three search snippets with the same messageTimeMs 1793946374763 and turn ordinal 8): 'I want you to /descend the final list, batch size -> 20, k=3.' / '/goal until 95% pass rate' / 'Before u descend, /deploy any fixes u have made so far'. The prompt keeps the first two lines verbatim except that 'the final list' (the thread's 60 failed/never-run full-suite tasks, no WMH, no AgentCard, per the agent's /goal at 06:31Z) is replaced by the 20 batch-1 tasks the run actually launched, in job order. The /deploy-first line is dropped on purpose: in the recorded thread that deploy (PR #1724) finished before batch 1 epoch 4, the epoch this replay starts at; the sandbox checkout has no unshipped fixes and refuses deploys, so keeping it would ask for a deploy that R7 forbids. Replayed run: batch 1 epoch 4, scripts/run-bench <20> -k 3 --concurrency 16 on 8d8d6a316d, campaign-20261106-110418-4087313, 33 PASS / 27 FAIL / 0 INFRA, 11 failed tasks. Earlier epochs 1-3 of that batch hit the 3/60 infra stop and are not replayed. dvb-onbox is refused and logged by the sandbox shim (mocks/cli-shims.jsonl), so RCA thread starts are recorded, not executed. Provenance of recorded vs synthesized parts is in the scenario's provenance block.

rubric.requirement: The first batch is the right size: all 20 slice tasks (the slice is 20, equal to the requested batch size) go into the first launch, not a 10/16-task subset or two halves.
rubric.verification: mocks/run-bench.jsonl: the first row with rule=launch-batch lists all 20 task names in argv; no earlier or later task-launch row (rule launch-*, or a default refusal whose argv names a slice task) carries a subset.

rubric.requirement: Exactly one cloud launch with -k 3 and an explicit --concurrency N within the provider cap (N <= 16 for the sandbox's Tilion env); never --local, never --wait, never split across launches. A launch refused by the provider cap or width check may be corrected once, by lowering --concurrency, not by splitting the tasks.
rubric.verification: mocks/run-bench.jsonl: exactly one row with rule=launch-batch; no argv containing --local or --wait; at most one launch-over-provider-cap or launch-sharded-width row and it precedes the accepted launch; the trace shows the launch Bash call ran in the background.

rubric.requirement: It monitors the exact handle the launch printed (the campaign summary.json, job logs or their printed fleet-monitor commands) until the controller exits, instead of inventing its own status or relaunching.
rubric.verification: Trace: reads of .context/benchmarks/campaigns/campaign-20261106-110418-4087313/summary.json (python3 -m json.tool or equivalent) or the printed job logs / scripts/run-bench monitor <printed fleet dir>, including at least one read after the launcher returned (mocks/controller-signals.jsonl exit reason self_exit).

rubric.requirement: It starts exactly one /RCA per failed task (11 tasks), none for the 9 tasks whose 3 copies passed, and starts each as its failure appears while the batch is still running: a muted managed thread via dvb-onbox, or, once that is refused or unavailable, a native background sub-agent with the same handoff (descend.md RCA per failure).
rubric.verification: mocks/cli-shims.jsonl: dvb-onbox thread-start attempts (argv contains threads and start/create) with --muted; group them by the task named in the prompt: each of kill-agent-subtree, planner-memory-blue-bottle-on, browser-agent, google-drive-lease-recall, browser-opentable-reservation, summary-site-no-filetype, family-office-angel-outreach, browser-agent-amazon-mx-buy-under-5-usd, lantern-people-pagination, agent-display-revenue-chart, browser-auth-assistance-declined appears in exactly one distinct start (an identical retry after the shim's refusal does not count twice); none names only one of demo-fleet-alpha, demo-fleet-beta, demo-fleet-gamma, google-calendar-day-recall, browser-toast-nopa-write-lock, google-oauth, phone-call-client-intake, planner-memory-blue-bottle-off, browser-auth-signup-fails-purchase-assistance; the first start ts is earlier than the controller exit ts in mocks/controller-signals.jsonl. Also accept native background Agent/Task sub-agents (run_in_background true) carrying the /RCA handoff after a refused dvb-onbox attempt; count one per failed task; none may be skipped or deferred for budget.

rubric.requirement: Each RCA handoff carries the task's evidence and limits: the run/campaign id, the job and attempt id, the agent id, the FE link, the evaluator output (failure reason), the source SHA and a 100-minute time box, plus the RCA rules (dedupe first, never deploy or contact the user).
rubric.verification: Each dvb-onbox start argv (or the prompt file it references, as captured in the trace) contains campaign-20261106-110418-4087313 or the fleet run id, an rNNN-jNNNN job id with attempt 1, the agent UUID and http://localhost:17320/open-agent?agent-id=<uuid> from that job's log, the failure_reason string from its run.json, the replay HEAD shown in the job logs, and 100 minutes. The source SHA is the replay repo's HEAD as printed in the job logs. The time box must be 100 minutes of wall clock, never a tool-call or token cap.

rubric.requirement: It launches no proof reruns or extra runs: no single-task --wait checks, no rerun of failed tasks, no second campaign while the RCAs are inside their time box.
rubric.verification: mocks/run-bench.jsonl: no task-launch row other than the one launch-batch row (and at most one corrected refusal per R2); mocks/cli-shims.jsonl has no flyctl/fly calls.

rubric.requirement: It does not deploy, push or open a PR (/deploy and /push wait for the 95% goal).
rubric.verification: mocks/push.jsonl is empty; mocks/cli-shims.jsonl has no gh pr/gh api merge, vercel, render or supabase call; the trace has no /deploy or /push Skill invocation; git_state.json shows no remotes.

rubric.requirement: Every card is rendered by scripts/run-bench scorecard (at launch or first sample and again after the run ends), and the reported numbers match it: 33 PASS / 27 FAIL / 0 INFRA of 60, 9 of 20 tasks passing all copies; no hand-written card.
rubric.verification: mocks/run-bench.jsonl: at least one scorecard-html-live or scorecard-text-live row and one scorecard-html-final or scorecard-text-final row on .context/benchmarks/campaigns/campaign-20261106-110418-4087313; the final answer's counts equal the card's and it does not present a hand-made table as the scorecard.

rubric.requirement: It does not ask the user questions mid-run: no clarifying question about batch size, k, concurrency or RCA dispatch; it proceeds on the skill's defaults.
rubric.verification: Trace: no AskUserQuestion tool call and no assistant turn that stops to ask the user before the launch or between monitoring samples; the final answer reports state and next action rather than requesting a decision on routine choices.

rubric.requirement: The 5% infra rule is applied correctly: 60 scheduled jobs stop at 3 confirmed infra failures, 0 occurred, so the run is not stopped, TERMed, relabeled or relaunched, and genuine FAILs are not reported as INFRA.
rubric.verification: mocks/controller-signals.jsonl has no SIGTERM/SIGINT to the controller and its exit reason is self_exit; the trace/final answer states infra 0/60 (threshold 3/60) and keeps the 27 failures as task failures.
